column8: Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 background, store first: backlist share of US print units rose from 51% (2004) to 71% (2022), read at source on NPD's slide; units for the whole market, not one author's dollars, so never as Laura's income mix.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-001 carried to 2023 (70%, a record, from the data owner's analyst); carry the 2023 figure there.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 or 3e area (2) at most: the 2009 split is Keel arithmetic on whole-percent shares and the card's own rounding ranges touch at -3.8%, so never about three times; say new books fell more than the backlist, or use Q96-006's direct BookScan figures.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the unit series behind rows 3, 5 and 6; 2011-12 falls are e-books and Borders, not the cycle.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; in the 2020 lockdown the backlist rose and new books fell (direction holds under the rounding); Laura's own 2020 breakout ran the other way (Q1-046), so never as her pattern.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 support at most: in 2022, when US shares fell 18.04% (checked in the repo's Damodaran file), new-book units fell 10.5% and the backlist 3.7%, direct BookScan figures with no rounding issue; units, a lockdown unwind, and Q1-030 and Q1-031 already carry the advance evidence.
Tue 17 Nov: store; supports Q1-049's single hit-driven holding (new books fell about 7.5% in 2019 while shares rose 31.21%); the 2018 inputs are not shown in rows 1 and 4, so list them before use.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the new-book slice shrank from 49% to 30% of units over twenty years, a trend in units, not author income.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.0 or 2.3, one sentence at most: Laura's own trade runs IPS l.11's split (PRH's CEO: the backlist gives latitude to take risks with new acquisitions); never a second extended mapping beside pencil and ink (CONCEIT guard, H8-046), and the publisher wants risk where her payments want none.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-009 (backlist as the publisher's cushion for advances), from the government's proposed findings, not the court; carry it as a second source there.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 mechanism, store first: an advance is priced from the publisher's sales forecast (court's words), so it moves on expectations like a share price; that it falls before sales do is Keel inference, never a finding; the court's market is advances of $250,000 or more.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (2): a court's figure (an advance can take three to four years to be paid) for why a downturn reaches the 2028 deposit late and only in part, beside Q12-033; say in the same downturn, not always the same months, never a lag rule (SKELETON 2.3).
Tue 17 Nov: store; about half of Hachette's books earn out, so for the rest the advance is all the book pays; Laura's own earn-out is not in the case.

Tue 17 Nov: store, or one clause in 2.3 if a judge asks whether a backlist could stand in for Treasuries: the catalogue's valuer held 8.5% while the 10-year went from 1.52% to 4.59% (checked in the repo FRED file); carry Q96-015's quote.
Tue 17 Nov: the fund's own words for Q96-014 (a long-term view on interest rates); carry the quote there.

Tue 17 Nov: store; disclosed sensitivity gives a catalogue about 16-17 years of duration (Keel arithmetic), longer than the ten payments' 9.94 and the holdings' 7.76 (NUMBERS 1 checked); the 2022 note's figures conflict, so 2023 only.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-016 from the second fund, with the same valuer firm, so it is not independent evidence.

Tue 17 Nov: false as used: a 50:50 debt-equity mix in a discount rate is the buyer's assumed financing, not a split of the catalogue's risk, so it never shows professionals price a creative asset as half bond, half stock.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a catalogue's cash flows are forecasts with growth sensitivities as large as the rate's; the KBRA wording is via MBW, not read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a rate court cut the catalogue's royalty income ($155.0m of value); books have no rate court, so no part needs it.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the market priced the catalogues about 50% below their marked values by Sep 2023; discounts also reflect fees and governance, so never all of it rates; carry Q96-022's vote.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-021 (owners acted on the price, 83.2% against continuing); partly a vote on governance.

Tue 17 Nov: store, the Hipgnosis reveal in one statement (a 26.3% cut at a 9.63% midpoint rate), read at source; if used, one clause that the steadiest-looking creative asset has no price until sold, never as a reason about Laura's own career.
Tue 17 Nov: Keel arithmetic splitting Q96-023's cut (about three-fifths rates); a linear extension past the disclosed 9.5%, so carry it there as rough.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Blackstone paid 24.7% under the last Citrin value and 10.3% over the new one in a competitive bid; carry Q96-029's Round Hill sale.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-027 (9.25% a month after 9.63%: the rate is a judgement); carry the offer document's figures there.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; three valuers, three prices in eleven months; the 8.25% or 8.50% conflict stands, and no conceit slot is free for it (2.3's turn is the eraser), never in Laura's words or a table.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; private catalogue multiples fell about a sixth from the 2019 peak; Shot Tower's own report not read and two 2022 figures conflict.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-025 (both listed catalogue funds sold below their valuers' figures).

Tue 17 Nov: store, or a 2.3 clause if a judge says a career can be sold: the backlist part can (Bowie bonds 1997, 7.9% against a 10-year near 6.3%-6.4%, checked in the repo FRED file), new advances cannot, which is the part IPS l.9 names; reported EMI guarantee noted.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the Bowie bonds fell to one notch above junk in 2004 while the 10-year sat at 3.80%; repayment in 2007 rests on secondary sources, not Moody's.

Tue 17 Nov: store, a creative-world instance for the reserve aha nobody can run on the plan (Laura borrows nothing): Chorion's covenant breach forced the Christie, Blyton and Mr Men sales; carry Q96-033's Hipgnosis covenant.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q96-032 (leverage turns a slow valuation fall into a forced choice).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the Dahl price is reported, not announced, and its revenue includes screen licences; serves no part.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a publisher's backlist at 1.8 times sales; sales are not royalties, so it says nothing about an author's share.

Tue 17 Nov: store; adds to Q12-027 (10% option fee) that the author writes the option, a small sure fee and a capped, rare purchase price; whether the case's licensing includes screen rights is not said.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; no audited exercise rate exists (guesses from under 1% to 10%), so never count options in any plan figure.

Tue 17 Nov: store; never in the same squeeze as shares: US shares rose 26.06% in 2023 (repo Damodaran file) while adaptation deals fell 53%; say when money cost more and studios struck; vendor method unstated.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; a creator's reversion right opens after 2052 for any grant Laura signs now, beyond every plan date.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 and 3e area (2), Client Knowledge: the case says the 2028 deposit comes from publishing advances, speaking engagements, licensing and other ventures (case text checked), the incomes IPS l.9 says come later and smaller, so the premise bites where the plan needs money; never the backlist never enters the portfolio (royalties may sit in other ventures, and licences can rest on old books).

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 wording guard: the counterbalance (IPS l.9, CANON A2) holds in dollars on dates held to the end, not in value: in 2022 the 10-year lost 17.83% and shares 18.04%, in 2008 +20.10% against -36.55% (repo Damodaran file checked); never the ladder rises when her career falls.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.3 at most as Q96-040's form (the deposit comes from the stock-like and option-like parts); never a replacement for IPS l.3's giant stock she can't sell, which CANON A1 leads with, nor a second extended mapping beside pencil and ink; near Q1b-025's two-part career.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, one clause of history if room: in 1970 saying a bond's yield is not what its holder earns drew outrage (Homer and Leibowitz's own preface), which is why IPS l.13's pay what they say is exactly true of coupons and face while the coupons' own interest is the open line; preface read as an extract.
Tue 17 Nov: the 1972 quote is secondary (a teaching site), so the plain definition comes from Becketti, read at source (Q104-027).

Tue 17 Nov: store; interest on interest by horizon for a 9% bond (Leibowitz 1979 via Ferguson); never beside NUMBERS 8a's 3.4%-15.3% as like for like (one bond's whole return against each $50,000 payment).

Tue 17 Nov: store or 3e area (1): Ferguson's $100m goal falls $18.4m short at two points less reinvestment; Laura's figures match NUMBERS 8a ($13,906 short at a flat 4.0%, $54,595 at zero, before the extra Treasuries).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, the disanalogy a dedication-minded judge raises: a cash-matched book escapes reinvestment only if every coupon goes straight to a payment, and Laura's cannot before 2033, which is why the extra Treasuries exist; say cash-flow matched, never not duration-matched (CANON C12); carry Q104-008.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.2 or 3a, store first: matching is easiest for a falling payment stream; Laura's is level and starts six years out, which is why her late rungs carry the most interest on interest (NUMBERS 8a).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a: anchor only on TNA l.5's reinvestment-rate risk (and WN l.18, l.24); drop IPS l.13's isn't dependent on yields staying put, which covers only the $2,388 top-up and the ten's price (coherence reader 6, H1; NUMBERS 2 box).
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q104-005 in Fabozzi's words (very little reinvestment risk when cash is paid out each month); carry the quote there.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the textbook trade-off (a conservative reinvestment rate costs more and risks less); the extra Treasuries are that conservative end.
Tue 17 Nov: the setup for Q104-011 (Fabozzi's 1992 book yielded 7.83% but assumed only 3%); carry it there.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a's why test at no interest, beside Q81's bill months: practice's cautious 3% of 1992 was breached for 42 months from Sep 2001 and in 217 of 407 months (rater reproduced on the repo DGS6MO); say the strictest standard found, then a fee below it, never below every assumption.
Tue 17 Nov: store; zero reinvestment as a working convention in a mortgage deal and bond indexes, beside the escrows' without reinvestment (Q54); chapter not noted, so cite Q54's sources first.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.2 or 3a: Bader's ideal of no selling and no reinvesting; Laura's book meets the first by holding to the end and the second's purpose because no payment depends on reinvesting; never that nothing is reinvested (WN l.18: reinvested coupons fund the rest, CANON A17).

Tue 17 Nov: store; Bader weighed zero reinvestment as a cost case when choosing what to prefund, not as a solvency test, so never zero was a named test in 1983; the professional test at zero is the escrow verifier's (Q54).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a parallel, not how they were sized (NUMBERS 2's linear programme): a distant contingency is covered by a modest reserve bought early; about 65% of the zero-interest gap falls in 2038-2042 (Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 8a) and $35,894 of extra Treasuries covers it.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a; fix the clash cell: the ten's own rungs pay only their own payments, but the extra Treasuries pool, paying the 2033-2036 gaps from later bonds' coupons and carrying the rest forward (NUMBERS 2 and 8a), so never no payment depends on another bond.
Tue 17 Nov: 2.2 store; dedicators feared calls in 1983; Laura's five T-bonds cannot be called (Q26-018), so the coupons are her only reinvestment exposure.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the 2042 rung carries 14.8% interest on interest against 2041's 15.3% (NUMBERS 8a checked); the bond was the latest available, not chosen for its coupon.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; 1983 actuaries valued dedicated books at 12-14%; a discussant's suggestion, serves no part.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3e area (1), outside authority beside Q104-042: a New York Fed sum shows the same 16% bond realises about 14.25% with coupons and 16% as a zero; zeros are history only, never a holding for Laura (STRIPS banned).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a cost of certainty: 1980s buyers gave up 40-100bp for life (partly call and tax protection); name each money year: $35,894 in January 2028 money, about $45,500 back in 1 January 2033 money if rates hold (NUMBERS 8h, 8k), never about $45,000 or most comes back.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; adds the reason to Q26-019 and H7-013: Treasury stopped issuing callables from February 1985 with the STRIPS programme.
Tue 17 Nov: store or a Table 1 note; stripping began against shrinking durations, Laura's 7.76 years against 9.94 (NUMBERS 1); say cash-flow matched, never not duration-matched (CANON C12).
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the first TIGRs (August 1982) drew over $1 billion of orders on the promise of no reinvesting; never a holding for Laura; carry Q104-026's date note.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; even the first receipts carried call risk on bonds callable from 2006; Laura's five T-bonds are the clean case (Q26-018).
Tue 17 Nov: date note for Q104-024: say August 1982 (NYT and Garbade), not Ferguson's July.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a, the plain definition if one is needed: a Kansas City Fed economist on 1981's 16% coupons that had to be reinvested at lower rates; stronger than Q16-011's handbook line; strips as history only.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; stripping was partly a tax trade before TEFRA 1982; taxes are out of the case's scope.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; $33.7bn stripped by Feb 1985 and STRIPS to $48.2bn by 1988, demand that includes tax trades.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e; certainty from holding to the date is true of a zero and of Laura's five T-bonds; her five iBond funds pay their net asset value, not a fixed sum (TNA l.13), so never for Laura's Treasuries alike.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; a 1985 newspaper sum where interest on interest is about two-thirds of a long zero's total value; its figures are inconsistent by about 2%.

Tue 17 Nov: store; falling rates made the same payments dearer to dedicate, IPS l.13's completion in another setting (NUMBERS 1 already shows it); the pension saving was against an actuarial rate.

Tue 17 Nov: the 1992 locked-in claim that Q104-042 tests; carry the quote there.
